findings.title: Tolgee staging API key leaked in public SPA bundle
findings.description: A Tolgee Project API Key (tgpak_...) is hardcoded in the production SPA JavaScript bundle served to all visitors. While testing confirmed the key is restricted to read-only metadata endpoints (all translation read/write endpoints return 403), it still exposes: the internal Tolgee project ID, the staging infrastructure hostname (tolgee.spiko.io), and organizational email (tech@spiko.tech). The key format and prefix reveal the translation management platform in use.
findings.impact: Low immediate risk due to restrictive permissions, but credential exposure in client-side code is a hygiene issue. If permissions are ever widened, the key is already public.
findings.remediation: Remove the API key from the SPA bundle. Serve translations as static JSON at build time or proxy through the backend API.

findings.title: Missing Content-Security-Policy header on app.spiko.io
findings.description: The main investor SPA at app.spiko.io does not return a Content-Security-Policy header. While the application uses DOMPurify for HTML sanitization, CSP provides defense-in-depth against XSS by restricting script sources, inline script execution, and other dangerous behaviors.
findings.impact: If any XSS vector is found in the future (e.g. a DOMPurify bypass, a new unsanitized rendering path), there is no CSP to limit its impact. Combined with the parent-domain cookie scope (F03), a successful XSS on any *.spiko.io subdomain could steal session cookies.
findings.remediation: Deploy a strict CSP with script-src restricted to known origins, no unsafe-inline, and no unsafe-eval.

findings.title: Parent-domain session cookie scope (.spiko.io)
findings.description: Session cookies are scoped to .spiko.io rather than the specific subdomain (app.spiko.io). This means any subdomain under spiko.io can read the session cookie.
findings.impact: Amplifier for any XSS or subdomain takeover finding. An attacker who compromises any *.spiko.io subdomain (including staging, PR previews, or vendor-delegated subdomains) can steal investor session tokens. Combined with missing CSP (F02) and the presence of staging/PR-preview wildcards in DNS, the attack surface is wider than necessary.
findings.remediation: Scope session cookies to the specific subdomain (app.spiko.io) using the Domain attribute. If cross-subdomain SSO is needed, use a dedicated auth flow rather than shared cookies.

findings.title: Missing HSTS header
findings.description: The application does not return a Strict-Transport-Security header. While Cloudflare enforces HTTPS at the edge, the browser does not know to always use HTTPS for this domain.
findings.impact: First-visit or cache-expired requests could be intercepted via MITM on an insecure network before the Cloudflare redirect fires. Low risk given Cloudflare edge enforcement, but HSTS is a simple defense-in-depth measure.
findings.remediation: Add Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload and consider HSTS preload submission.

findings.title: Admin RBAC permission matrix exposed in public SPA bundle
findings.description: The full Role-Based Access Control permission matrix is embedded in the production SPA bundle, including role names (super-admin, compliance, tech, etc.), all permission strings, and the mapping of which roles have which permissions. This reveals the internal authorization architecture to any visitor.
findings.impact: Aids an attacker in understanding the internal role hierarchy and targeting privilege escalation. Knowing exact permission names helps craft targeted IDOR or authorization bypass attempts against the admin API.
findings.remediation: Move the RBAC matrix server-side. Send only the authenticated user's own permissions to the client.

findings.title: Questionnaire name enumeration via error messages
findings.description: API error responses for invalid questionnaire submissions include an enum of valid questionnaire names (5 values). This reveals internal business logic naming conventions.
findings.impact: Minimal direct impact. Provides reconnaissance value for targeted API fuzzing.
findings.remediation: Return generic error messages that do not enumerate valid values.

findings.title: Marketing email preferences default-subscribed (potential GDPR Art. 7 concern)
findings.description: During account registration, marketing email preferences appear to be opted-in by default rather than requiring explicit consent. GDPR Article 7 requires freely given, specific, informed consent for marketing communications.
findings.impact: Regulatory risk. Pre-checked consent boxes do not meet GDPR standards for valid consent in the EU.
findings.remediation: Ensure marketing communications require explicit opt-in (unchecked by default) with clear description of what the user is consenting to.

findings.title: EBICS banking endpoint exposed without WAF
findings.description: The EBICS 3.0 banking protocol endpoint at ebics.preprod.spiko.io is served directly through AWS ELB (via Qovery/criom.sh) without Cloudflare WAF protection, unlike all other Spiko services. The endpoint is directly accessible on the internet.
findings.impact: The EBICS endpoint lacks the rate limiting, bot protection, and WAF rules that protect all other Spiko services. An attacker can directly probe the EBICS XML endpoint without Cloudflare interference. EBICS is a banking protocol that handles financial transactions.
findings.remediation: Route ebics.preprod.spiko.io through Cloudflare to gain WAF/rate-limiting coverage, or restrict access to known banking partner IP ranges via AWS security groups.

findings.title: Configuration drift on .finance mirror domain
findings.description: The spiko.finance domain appears to be a mirror/alternate domain for the spiko.io platform, sharing the same staging wildcard certificate. However, the .finance mirror shows configuration drift: investor-auth.spiko.finance returns NXDOMAIN (while investor-auth.spiko.io works), and the /v0/ API gateway prefix may not be configured on the .finance API host.
findings.impact: Inconsistent configuration between mirrors may create gaps where security controls present on .io are absent on .finance. If the .finance domain is publicly accessible, it could provide a less-protected entry point.
findings.remediation: Either fully deprecate the .finance mirror or ensure parity with .spiko.io for all security controls.

findings.title: Internal organizational email disclosed via Tolgee API key metadata
findings.description: The Tolgee API key metadata endpoint reveals the organizational email tech@spiko.tech, which is not publicly listed elsewhere. This provides a valid email target for social engineering.
findings.impact: Minimal direct technical impact. Useful for targeted phishing or social engineering against the engineering team.
findings.remediation: Restrict the /v2/api-keys/current metadata endpoint or redact user information from the response.

tested_and_clean: IDOR on investor-api /v0/ endpoints (account, user, settings) - returns only own data
Tolgee API key write access - all write endpoints return 403, key is read-only metadata only
Tolgee translation read access - returns 403, cannot retrieve or modify translations
XSS via SPA bundles - DOMPurify sanitization in place, no unprotected dangerouslySetInnerHTML in application code
XSS via Tolgee translation injection - key cannot write translations, read endpoints also blocked
Impersonation token brute force - /v0/impersonation/redeem requires UUID, computationally infeasible
